source: Netball Skills and Conditioning Manual, Level 1, 3rd version, Niel du Plessis and Erin Burger, Catching section, page 71. The manual describes this drill exactly as the pull-in drill except for the fourth instruction: pass the ball straight back to the passer, without pulling the ball to the body. The cues are the manual's. The numeric bands are NOT, and are PROVISIONAL until a coach sets them.

checkpoints.cue: Show the passer your arm span, the range your hands can reach.
checkpoints.why: The passer may put the ball anywhere inside that span, so the span must be presented honestly.

checkpoints.cue: Wide base power position, static with the feet.
checkpoints.why: The manual keeps the feet still and makes the hands and arms do the work.

checkpoints.cue: React to the front, in front of your shoulder.
checkpoints.why: Taking the ball in front of the shoulder line is what gives the arms room to control it.

checkpoints.cue: Both hands on the ball together.
checkpoints.why: Two hands give the control needed to send a strong ball back.

checkpoints.cue: Control it, but do not pull it in to your body.
checkpoints.why: This is the whole difference between this drill and the pull-in. A ball brought to the chest here has failed the drill, not passed it.

checkpoints.cue: Stay tall. The hands work, the body does not.
checkpoints.why: The worker is static with the feet and uses hands and arms only.

checkpoints.cue: Pass it straight back from where you caught it.
checkpoints.why: The ball leaves from in front of the shoulder, which is the fastest release available.

checkpoints.cue: Send it back in front of the shoulder, not from the chest.
checkpoints.why: A pass that starts at the chest has already lost the time the drill exists to save.
